rows.verified: The Display Screen Equipment Regulations apply to workers who use DSE daily for continuous periods of one hour or more.
Employers must carry out a DSE workstation assessment for covered users.
Employers must reduce DSE risks, including by providing breaks or changes of activity.
Employers must arrange and pay for an eye and eyesight test when a DSE user requests one.
DSE users must receive health and safety training and information about risks and safe working practices.
Short, frequent breaks are preferable to longer, less frequent breaks for intensive DSE work.
There is no single legal duration or frequency for DSE breaks; arrangements depend on the work.
Employers must provide special glasses where an eye test shows they are needed only for the DSE viewing distance.
DSE controls depend on workstation design, equipment, posture, work duration, environment, user needs and work organisation.
DSE evidence is workstation- and user-specific and is not an exact parcel-level musculoskeletal or visual-strain probability.
A pressure system contains or is likely to contain a relevant fluid at pressure above 0.5 bar.
Pressure equipment must be safe, suitable for its intended purpose and installed, modified and repaired correctly.
Users must know the operating conditions, fluid characteristics and safe operating limits of pressure equipment.
Suitable protective devices such as safety valves or bursting discs must be correctly set and kept functional.
Pressure systems require suitable maintenance based on system age, use and operating environment.
People operating, installing, maintaining, repairing, inspecting or testing pressure equipment need appropriate skills, knowledge and refresher training.
Most pressure systems require a written scheme of examination prepared or certified by a competent person.
Statutory examination under the written scheme does not replace routine inspection and maintenance.
Pressure-system controls depend on the fluid, pressure, equipment, protective devices, installation, operating limits and examination history.
Pressure-system evidence is equipment-, fluid- and operating-condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level rupture probability.
